name: p5-v1

scanner.code_tree: the commit of this file, synced to /scratch/$USER/kestrix-sys/code-final (scanner identical to dev run r1, df9248d)
scanner.frozen: no scanner change after this file; tuned on dev only (two widenings measured and rejected: format strings followed by arguments, +2 pairs for +677 alerts; copies into any destination, +13 pairs for +1,209 alerts)

comparison_tools.name: flawfinder
comparison_tools.licence: GPL-2.0-or-later, run as an external program, never vendored
comparison_tools.mode: flawfinder --csv . on each shard, default minimum level 1, offline

comparison_tools.name: opengrep with opengrep-rules
comparison_tools.licence: engine LGPL-2.1; rules LGPL-2.1 with the Commons Clause
comparison_tools.mode: every rule of the c, rust and swift folders, one run per shard, offline (its C rules do not read C++ files)

data.source: CVEfixes v1.0.8 (CC BY 4.0), C, C++, Rust and Swift file changes of fix commits, filters of the code benchmark
data.split: project-disjoint, seeded hash kestrixcodebench-v1, 30% of groups to test

claims_to_check: C and C++: flawfinder is expected to detect far more than Kestrix (it reports every risky call at its default level); Kestrix's alerts per KLOC on fixed files are expected to be below flawfinder's and opengrep's.
C and C++: Kestrix alerts per KLOC on fixed files stay within the dev interval [0.05, 0.14].
C and C++: Kestrix detection is reported next to opengrep's with the paired bootstrap interval; no direction is claimed (equal on dev).
Rust (14 in-scope test pairs) and Swift (1) are too small to support any claim; their numbers are reported as measured.
Reported as measured whatever the outcome; no rule or threshold changes follow this run.
metrics: detection (family match within 3 lines of a changed line), fix-aware, fix-weighted, alerts per KLOC on after-files; 95% percentile bootstrap, 1000 resamples of whole repositories
